item.title: The Chemical Brothers’ ‘Go’ Sees 429% Streaming Surge After ‘Apex’ Synch
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to Trending Tunes, the podcast where we dive into the latest music news and trends. I'm your host, [Name], and today we're talking about a major streaming boost for The Chemical Brothers' 2015 track "Go".
[Music transitions to a clip of "Go" by The Chemical Brothers]
Host: You might have heard "Go" recently in the new Netflix thriller Apex, starring Charlize Theron and Taron Egerton. The song's featured in a pivotal scene where the heroine is being hunted by the villain, and it's had a huge impact on the song's streaming numbers.
According to Luminate, "Go" saw a 429% streaming boost in the week following the film's release, with over 487,000 total U.S. on-demand streams between April 24-30. That's a significant increase from the 92,000 streams it had in the week prior.
[Music transitions back to the host]
Host: But what's even more interesting is how the song ended up in the film. Director Baltasar Kormákur revealed in an interview that it was Taron Egerton who suggested "Go" for the scene. And despite some initial hesitation from the team, the song ultimately won them over.
Host: "Go" is also currently sitting at number 5 on the Dance Digital Song Sales chart, and Apex is at number 1 on Netflix's weekly top 10 global films and series. The song, which features vocals from Q-Tip, was originally released in 2015 as part of The Chemical Brothers' album Born in the Echoes.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Thanks for tuning in to Trending Tunes. If you want to hear more about the latest music trends and news, be sure to subscribe to our podcast and follow us on social media. [Outro music continues to play until the end]
